families.s: HSE papermaking-machine and associated-task safety guidance
families.t: process sequence, machinery hazards, access, nips, stored energy, threading, cleaning, maintenance and safe intervention
f: HSE's papermaking guidance covers both machinery and associated tasks through the process.
Risk assessment should address the papermaking sequence rather than isolated machine components only.
Roller nips, drives, reels and moving webs require effective safeguarding.
Threading, broke removal and cleaning can require planned safe access.
Stored mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, steam and electrical energy should be controlled before intervention.
Maintenance arrangements should preserve guards, interlocks and emergency controls.
Operators and maintenance workers need process-specific competence and instructions.
Changes to speed, product, equipment or work method should trigger review of safeguards and safe systems.
families.g: Papermaking risk depends on machine sequence, speed and web tension, nips and reels, heat and steam, access and intervention, isolation, maintenance and competence.

families.s: HSE safe use of paper reeling and slitting machines
families.t: parent reels, unwind stands, web threading, slitting, winding, reel handling, guards, safe operating procedures and intervention
f: Reeling and slitting machines mount a parent reel at an unwind stand.
The process creates hazards from rotating reels, moving webs, nip points and slitting knives.
Reel loading and handling should use suitable equipment and controlled methods.
Guards should prevent access to dangerous moving parts during normal running.
Threading, splice work and setting should use safe operating procedures.
Intervention for breaks, jams or defects should stop movement and control stored energy.
Slitting blades require safe adjustment, handling and disposal.
Training, supervision and maintenance should support the documented safe system.
families.g: Rewinding and slitting risk depends on reel mass and speed, web tension, nip and blade exposure, reel handling, threading and intervention, guarding, isolation and competence.

families.s: HSE power-operated paper-cutting guillotine safety guidance
families.t: high-risk machinery, blade and clamp, guards, controls, isolation, training, maintenance, blade changing and contractor access
f: Power-operated paper-cutting guillotines are high-risk machines with a history of serious accidents.
Operators require specific training in safe use.
The blade and clamping system should be protected by effective safeguards and controls.
Guards and safety devices should be inspected and maintained.
The machine should be isolated before access to the danger area for maintenance or repair.
Blade changing and handling require a planned method, suitable tools and competent people.
Contractors and service engineers should receive machine-specific isolation and access information.
Unsafe safeguards, control faults or evidence of bypassing should stop use until corrected.
families.g: Guillotine risk depends on blade and clamp force, guard and control integrity, workpiece handling, blade changing, isolation, maintenance, training and supervision.

families.s: HSE paper-industry manual-handling and mechanical-aid guidance
families.t: reels, bales, board stacks, broke, awkward loads, task assessment, trolleys, hoists, grabs and redesign
f: Paper-sector handling tasks include moving reels, bales, board stacks, broke and machinery parts.
The size and shape of a paper product can create risk even where weight alone is not excessive.
Task assessment should identify ways to avoid or reduce hazardous manual handling.
Mechanical grabs can eliminate repeated loose-broke handling.
Stands and simple supports can reduce awkward core and shaft handling.
Trolleys and lifting aids can reduce handling of drums, rolls and raw materials.
Task redesign should reduce carrying distance, reach, twisting and repetitive effort.
Handling controls should be reviewed after injury, process change or introduction of new reel or product sizes.
families.g: Paper handling risk depends on load mass, size and shape, grip and stability, frequency and distance, posture and reach, floor and space, mechanical aids, staffing and task design.

families.s: HSE paper-mill combustible-material and process-fire risk guidance
families.t: paper and dust fuel, ignition, hot work, process heating, storage, housekeeping, detection, fire separation and emergency response
f: HSE lists specific guidance on fire risk in paper mills.
Paper, board, broke and dust can provide substantial combustible fuel.
Ignition controls should cover hot work, heaters, electrical faults, friction and overheating machinery.
Housekeeping should limit accumulations of paper waste and combustible dust.
Storage layout should support separation, access and firefighting.
Process and maintenance changes should be assessed for new fire hazards.
Detection, alarm, escape and emergency arrangements should reflect rapid fire and smoke spread.
Fire precautions should be coordinated with machine isolation and safe shutdown.
families.g: Paper-mill fire risk depends on combustible inventory and dust, ignition and hot work, machinery heat and friction, storage and separation, housekeeping, detection, escape and emergency response.
